claim_1.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 212 vaccinated subjects across five influenza vaccine seasons showed that day 28 influenza antibody responses decreased with increasing age compared to younger vaccinees.

sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age (Figures 1B, 1C, and S1C), consistent with previous studies (Seidman et al., 2012).

comparison.finding: day 28 influenza antibody responses decreased with increasing age; elderly subjects had lower antibody responses than younger vaccinees

claim_2.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 212 vaccinated subjects across five influenza vaccine seasons showed that vaccines from different seasons induced varying magnitudes of HAI responses compared to other influenza seasons, with the 2010 season generating the strongest responses.

sources.quote: Vaccines from different seasons induced varying levels of HAI responses, and there was a significant decrease in the response with age (Figure 1C). Subjects vaccinated during the 2010 season, the year after the H1N1 2009 pandemic, generated the strongest HAI responses.

comparison.finding: subjects vaccinated during the 2010 season generated the strongest HAI responses compared to other influenza seasons

claim_3.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 62 vaccinees measured through day 180 showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 and declined significantly by day 180 compared to day 28 after vaccination.

sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A).

comparison.finding: antibody responses declined significantly by day 180 compared to the peak at day 28 after vaccination

claim_4.claim: hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays analysis of plasma from 62 vaccinees measured at day 28 and day 180 showed that day 180 antibody titers depended significantly on the original day 28 response compared to lower initial day 28 responses.

sources.quote: Because the D180 antibody titer shows significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28 (Figure 6B), examining the molecular profile associated with the D180 response would identify many of the mechanisms responsible for generating the D28 response.

comparison.finding: day 180 antibody titer showed significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28

claim_41.claim: miRNA expression profiling analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010-season vaccinees, integrated with transcriptomic profiling and TargetScan predictions, showed that the antiviral interferon signature module M75 on day 1 after vaccination had potential novel miRNA regulators including miR-424 targeting OAS3 and CXCL10 compared to genes without these predicted negative miRNA correlations.

sources.quote: Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature (Figure 7E) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response. This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424. This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation (Samuel, 2001), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes (Dufour et al., 2002).
